title: The Tuck Rule
setup: January 19, 2002, an AFC divisional playoff game in the snow. The Patriots have the ball at the Raiders' 42-yard line with 1:50 left, trailing 13-10. Tom Brady pump-fakes, tucks the ball back toward his body, and Raiders cornerback Charles Woodson knocks it loose. Linebacker Greg Biekert recovers it, and everyone on the field treats it as a fumble. Referee Walt Coleman heads to the replay monitor.
question: What does Coleman rule?
options: Incomplete pass. Patriots keep the ball.
ruling: Coleman reversed the call: "The quarterback's arm was coming forward." The Patriots kept the ball, Adam Vinatieri kicked a 43-yard field goal to tie the game, and another in overtime to win it.
rulebookNote: Rule 3, Section 21, Article 2: any intentional forward movement of the thrower's arm starts a forward pass, even if the ball is lost while tucking it back.
